I need to preface this by saying that the following particular system would only apply to big/default subs and not smaller subs with specific-names that a user made because they had an idea they liked.

There needs to be a system in place that publicly logs information when mods take any administrative action such as banning a user, as well as a system that enables the userbase to get rid of mods if they've stopped caring about quality. This way, if a mod makes a call, the community can give them feedback to either praise them for getting rid of a troll or to give them criticism for being arbitrary and/or tyrannical. This would also apply to rule changes that nobody asked for. A system like this would be pretty important because it would stop mods from carelessly moderating their subs and making the experience less enjoyable for the community.

A system like this would not apply to smaller, specifically-named subs because that would be a problem. Subs with general names like /v/dogs or /v/cats are expected to be general subs about dogs and cats. If both of those subs go to shit because the mods got out of hand, well it's their sub, right? Now the reason why this system wouldn't apply to smaller, specifically-named subs is that these kinds of subs are usually made by one user that had an idea that they liked and they wanted to make a sub about it. If this system was implemented, then trolls could waltz on in there and abuse the system to get rid of the one mod. This system also wouldn't apply to smaller, specifically-named subs because in this scenario making a separate specifically-named sub would actually be a viable solution.
